Fark, Slashdot, Digg, Reddit... We all know the litany of failed or failing sites. We also know that many failures arise when site owners attempt to monetize the site's value. For example, Reddit's current moves towards stifling discussion on several topics seem to have been motivated by a desire to make the site more acceptable to investors, who presumably see commercial disadvantages to being linked to "fat people hate" and similar sentiments. Some people on Voat are already suggesting that sooner or later the list of failed sites will be updated to read "Fark, Slashdot, Digg, Reddit... and Voat", as sooner or later /u/Atko, /u/PuttItOut and any other site owners will also introduce unpopular changes to the site as they attempt to "cash out". I suggest we try to avoid this.

Don't get me wrong, I'm not opposed to money or the monetization of Voat, so long as it's done well. Atko, PuttItOut and perhaps others whom I don't know have put a lot of work into Voat, and should be extremely well rewarded for this - I have no objection to Atko becoming a millionaire many times over. He set this place up and is working to keep it going, and deserves to make something in return. If we can find a way for Atko (and PuttItOut and everyone else involved in setting up and running the site) to get rich from Voat without stifling free speech or introducing unpopular changes - that is, if we can work with Atko to (a) build the best, most open site we can, and (b) make Atko rich - it will be less likely that Voat will one day go the way of its predecessors.

I feel that the best way forward is for us, the ordinary Voaters, to offer to collaborate with Atko in making Voat highly profitable, whilst avoiding the errors we can see happening at other sites. I suggest we set up a team to do this, with the team's three equal aims being "to help Atko make money out of Voat", "to preserve free speech in Voat and elsewhere on the internet" and "to build the best tools for free and open discourse of any website". We have a number of advantages:

  • Voaters are, I suspect, on average smarter and better educated than the users of some other sites (see Alexa for details).
  • Given this, we are probably earning above average for our demographic cohorts (or will be once we start work).
  • We are more than averagely sensitive to issues around free speech and individual liberty.
  • These provide Voat with a distinct demographic. Compare our front page with Reddit's - we are often more serious, and we are certainly more engaged with politics and technology issues. For some businesses, particularly those that seek to build long-term relationships with discriminating clients, people like us are highly desirable customers. We are monetizable.
  • We've seen what's happened at other sites, so both we and Atko know some of the mistakes to avoid.
  • No other site has a team dedicated to avoiding "monetization errors". There are thousands and thousands of Voaters, and even if only a small fraction of us are involved in such a team we will already have more eyeballs and more brains focused on ways for Atko to make money, and ways for us to get the site we want, than Reddit or any similar discussion forum. We can help Atko and the rest of the Voat team avoid Reddit's mistakes, and collaborate to build a great community.

Exactly how this project might move forward is up for discussion, of course. I might be the only person who thinks this way, or perhaps there are good reasons for not setting up such a team. But if there are other people who think that this is a good idea - that collaborating with Atko on monetization of Voat is the best way to ensure Voat's long-term survival as a place for free and open discussion - perhaps we might discuss things further. My hope is that we can build the commercial realities of running a site like Voat into our culture's DNA, so that Voat avoids the problems other sites have met. We are smart, socially-involved people, and there are thousands of us: let's use our advantages now to build the best possible future for Voat, for Atko, for ourselves, and for every other person who wants or needs a place to talk freely and openly, without being stifled or repressed.

Sorry, I'm slow to respond. I have been supporting Citrix since it was called Winframe, and ran on its own specialized version of Windows NT 3.51. Yikes, I feel old.

From an architectural perspective, the features of Microsoft's native Windows Terminal Services have been slowly catching up to where Citrix Metaframe/XenApp are. Citrix's real advantage is its platform independent ICA client, which runs natively in Windows, IOS, Java, Android, etc. The problem is the Citrix Receiver has become fairly bloated and problematic to support in my opinion. There are several open source RDP clients that work in the IOS/ Android /Linux space as well,

The latest XenApp 7.6 release is a bit of a mess. Citrix had through that applicaiton virtualization was going away, and focused on desktop virtualization, XenDesktop. They have basically thrown away the old XenApp 6.5 and previous design manage consoles, and design, and replaced it with a bloated mess XenDesktop. You need multiple SQL servers, you need a full active directory, you need dedicated load balancer (netscaler) if you wish to you SSL. In a VM based environment the ability to add a box is fairly simple, but there is a cost to supporting more systems. If your requirements are small, I honestly don't think Citrix is your best choice. If you have an enterprise which needs hundreds of simultaneous users, then Citrix might justify the high cost of licenses.
